description: Family 5: Jade — young single parent, age 18-20, first-year apprentice. Not on Universal Credit. One child (Alfie, age 11 months) in private nursery. Tests: apprentice minimum earnings threshold (£120.80/week), working parent entitlement for under-2s (available from 9 months), Tax-Free Childcare on low apprentice wages, single parent work test.

costEstimate.description: Worked example for Jade. Jade is an 18-20 year old first-year apprentice earning above the apprentice minimum earnings threshold of £120.80 per week. As a single parent, only Jade needs to meet the work test. Alfie is 11 months old and over the 9-month threshold for the working parent entitlement. The Sunderland government under-2 funding rate (£10.30/hr) far exceeds the provider's effective rate (£6.40/hr), eliminating any shortfall.

alfie.narrative: Alfie attends Little Stars Day Nursery (provider_27) for 4 morning sessions per week. The nursery operates 50 weeks per year. Each morning session is 5 hours at £32.00 per session for under-2s, giving an effective hourly rate of £6.40/hr. At 11 months old, Alfie is over the 9-month threshold and eligible for 15 funded hours per week. The government under-2 funding rate (£10.30/hr) far exceeds the provider's effective rate (£6.40/hr), meaning zero shortfall to the parent.

selections.source: provider_27 (Little Stars Day Nursery, under-2 rate: £32.00/morning session)

step1_childcareFees.note: Using provider_27 under-2 rate: £32.00 per morning session, 5 hours per session

step3_fundedHoursReduction.scheme: Working parent entitlement (under 2, available from 9 months)
step3_fundedHoursReduction.eligibilityNote: Jade is a first-year apprentice earning above £120.80/week (the apprentice minimum earnings threshold). As a single parent, only she needs to meet the work test. Alfie is 11 months — over the 9-month age threshold.
step3_fundedHoursReduction.shortfallNote: The Sunderland government under-2 funding rate (£10.30/hr) far exceeds the provider's effective rate (£6.40/hr). The provider retains the excess.

step4_unfundedHours.note: Total weekly hours: 4 mornings × 5 hrs = 20 hrs/week. During 38 term weeks, 15 funded, 5 unfunded. During 12 non-term weeks, all 20 unfunded.

totalCostOfChildcare.description: The total annual cost of all childcare for this family, before any government support is applied.

fundedHours.note: Government pays 15 hrs × £10.30 × 38 wks = £5,871.00 to provider. Parent saves 15 hrs × £6.40 × 38 wks = £3,648.00. The £2,223 difference is because the government rate (£10.30/hr) far exceeds the provider's rate (£6.40/hr).

taxFreeChildcare.note: 20% × £2,752.00 = £550.40 (under £2,000 cap). Registered childcare costs paid by parent after funded hours: £6,400 - £3,648 = £2,752.

familyTotal.summaryNote: Jade's childcare costs £6,950 per year (including meals and consumables). Government support totals £4,198 (60% of total cost). After funded hours and Tax-Free Childcare, Jade pays approximately £2,752. The Sunderland under-2 funding rate (£10.30/hr) far exceeds the provider rate (£6.40/hr), eliminating any shortfall. Compared to an equivalent scenario in Oxford (£4,140), Jade pays significantly less — driven by lower nursery fees in Sunderland.

apprenticeContext.description: First-year apprentices have a lower minimum earnings threshold for childcare scheme eligibility.

ageThresholdNote.description: The working parent entitlement for under-2s is only available from when the child reaches 9 months old. Alfie was born in March 2025 and turned 9 months in December 2025. If Jade had needed childcare before December 2025, no funded hours would have been available.
